candidates.primary_child_content:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

![](https://www.wsws.org/asset/2c3adca7-71f8-4bce-9946-debc28c84ae1?rendition=image1280)

Although this dynamic is often seen as encompassing the band’s overall sound, Cobain and the others possessed an undeniable ear for pop-sensible melodies. The underlying rhythm and bass sections work as a tandem in many instances, driving the music forward into Cobain’s more raucous crescendos.

This dynamic can be seen on songs such as the band’s break-out single “Smells like Teen Spirit”. “I find it hard/It’s hard to find/Oh well, whatever, never mind” goes the lyric of Cobain’s final verse. Feelings of disgust and angst at the existing world (“Here we are now, entertain us/I feel stupid and contagious/Here we are now, entertain us”), feelings that clearly struck a chord with a wider audience, and a willingness to buck convention prevail throughout, as each wailed chorus strongly punctuates and underscores these sentiments. From the titling of the song to its content, “Smells…” can be seen as a reference point for many of Nirvana’s strengths and weaknesses.

The title, at the time mistakenly taken from a brand of deodorant, was reportedly given to the song because Cobain thought it had a “revolutionary” sound to it. Emerging from the West Coast American punk scene of the mid-to-late 1980s, Cobain was familiar with various forms of middle class radicalism, for a time dating feminist “riot grrl” rocker Tobi Vail. For better or worse, these influences (opposition to sexism, racism and homophobia) certainly had their place in the band’s own formation.

“In Bloom” expresses the group’s desire to distance themselves from attempts to identify their music with the mostly aggressive and hedonistic imagery found in popular culture. The song criticizes individuals who “like all our pretty songs” and “like to shoot [their] gun,” but ultimately “don’t know what it means.”

“Come As You Are” contains such lyrics as: “Come, doused in mud/Soaked in bleach/As I want you to be,” with the song’s bridge possessing the provocative refrain “And I swear that I don’t have a gun.” The song’s instrumental is perhaps the catchiest on the album, with a water-like effect placed on the electric guitar that immediately draws the listener in.

Of particular note is the song “Lithium”. Intended as a depiction of religious fundamentalism and the closed-mindedness that it breeds, Cobain scathingly sings “I’m so happy/ ‘Cause today I found my friends/They’re in my head…And just maybe/ I’m to blame for all I’ve heard.” Cobain’s sarcasm is particularly biting here.

The use of sarcasm to depict the effects of religious “lithium” here also, however, points to a deeper cynicism, fueled by the artist’s own experience with “born-again” Christianity in his youth. As though simply reviling a thing were enough to get rid of it, the mocking perhaps makes up for a lack of clarity on the subject. Cobain fails to communicate how such a thing as religious obscurantism continues to have such a hold on social life, and why the artist himself may have fallen into its clutches at an earlier time. In general, processes and trends that disturb the artist are vividly identified, but not explored.

candidates.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
candidates.primary_child_content:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

candidates.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
candidates.primary_child_content:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

items.title: Assessing an American pop icon
items.exact_text:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

items.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
items.exact_text:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

return.content:
Assessing an American pop icon > Assessing an American pop icon > Nick Barrickman5 December 2012

- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

return.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
return.content:
Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > The end, but not the end

Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

return.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
return.content:
Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > Anarchy in the UK

The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

items.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
items.exact_text:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

items.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
items.exact_text:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

retrieved_docs.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
retrieved_docs.content:
Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > The end, but not the end

Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

retrieved_docs.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
retrieved_docs.content:
Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died > Anarchy in the UK

The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

sources.title: Assessing an American pop icon
sources.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

citations.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
citations.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

citations.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
citations.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

metadata.source_evidence_content:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

evidence_history.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
evidence_history.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

evidence_history.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
evidence_history.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

last_result.narrative:
Pixies 这条世界线可以从一个核心事实开始：目录数据显示，这个艺人实体下关联着 102 张专辑与 1619 首音乐作品，规模远超“生涯只有六年”这一描述给人的直觉印象 [music-api:artist:98542]。这种数量与时间跨度之间的张力，本身就是继续沿图探索的理由——它提示我们，Pixies 的目录里既有核心录音室作品，也可能包含大量现场、合辑与再版，值得逐条展开。

从年代与场景来看，目录中的艺人简介把 Pixies 定位为上世纪 80 年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，并提到他们属于 4AD 旗下，音乐融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和 Surf Rock，标志性风格是粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏、和谐的男女合声，以及隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词 [music-api:artist:98542]。同一段简介还指出，他们当时被主流媒体拒之门外，最终因乐队领袖 Black Francis 与贝斯手兼歌手 Kim Deal 的矛盾而在 92 年解体 [music-api:artist:98542]。这些信息共同勾勒出一个“地下/另类场景出身、商业主流接受度有限、内部张力导致终止”的叙事框架，也解释了为什么图中的歌曲节点值得逐一查看：它们正是这一风格与场景的具体载体。

图中的歌曲节点覆盖了不同面向。Where Is My Mind? 与 Where Is My Mind 作为两个独立条目同时存在，都通过 performed_by 关系指向 Pixies [music-api:artist:98542]；这种同曲异名或不同版本并存的情况，本身就是目录层面值得留意的细节。Here Comes Your Man、Hey、The Thing、The Happening、Greens and Blues、All I Think About Now 同样以 performed_by 关系挂在 Pixies 之下 [music-api:artist:98542]。把这些节点放在一起，可以看到一条从早期代表作到较晚作品的目录切片，适合作为继续探索的入口。

影响关系是这条世界线中最值得展开的部分。图中有一条从 Pixies 指向 Nirvana 的 influenced 边 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。外部资料对此有更具体的说法：Nirvana 受到 The Melvins，尤其是美国朋克乐队 The Pixies 的影响 [knowledge:chunk:21ba719d1d12c13424cc0502]；另有资料称 Pixies 对 Nirvana 有深远影响，并且 Pixies 在英国拿下三张前十专辑，而在美国连 Billboard 前 60 都尚未进入 [knowledge:chunk:8d38574abe1b22543e32da12]。这组对比说明，Pixies 的影响力路径并不是先在本土主流取得成功、再向外辐射，而更像是在英国等市场先获得认可，再通过后来者对美国另类摇滚产生回响。

把这条影响边放回更大的场景中，还能看到另一层关系：有资料在讨论 Nirvana 的遗产时提出，如果不是 Nirvana，也会有另一支站在 REM、Pixies、The Replacements 和 Sonic Youth 等“巨人”肩上的乐队翻过那道把地下与主流隔开的墙 [knowledge:chunk:9994c86ab814a3c2b8e64546]。同一资料还提到，Nirvana 与 grunge 的崛起在 1994 年的英国产生了反向效果，Britpop 随之兴起 [knowledge:chunk:8d38574abe1b22543e32da12]。这意味着 Pixies 在图中的位置不只是一个被指向的源头，而是连接美国另类摇滚与英国场景变化的一个节点，值得沿着 influenced 边继续追踪。

综合来看，这条世界线的探索价值在于三层叠加：目录层面有 102 张专辑、1619 首作品和多个具体歌曲节点可供展开 [music-api:artist:98542]；风格与场景层面有 4AD、朋克/Indie/Surf Rock 融合、男女合声与片断式歌词等可核实的描述 [music-api:artist:98542]；影响层面则有指向 Nirvana 的明确边，以及关于英美市场接受度差异和 Britpop 反向效应的外部叙述 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d][knowledge:chunk:8d38574abe1b22543e32da12]。沿着这些节点与关系继续走，可以把“一支短命乐队为何被反复提及”这个问题拆解成可验证的目录事实与可追溯的影响链条。

sources.title: Assessing an American pop icon
sources.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

citations.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
citations.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

citations.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
citations.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

metadata.description: Pixies是上世纪80年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，关于他们对后来Grunge音乐的影响，人们最常听到的评论就是：“It's hard to imagine Nirvana without the Pixies。”（很难想象没有Pixies乐队Nirvana会不会存在。）不过作为4AD旗下的一个传奇乐队，其音乐影响还包括8、90年代的Britpop和Indie rock。虽然Pixies的音乐生涯并不长（6年），但他们无疑是最具革新精神的乐队之一——粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏与和谐的男、女合声交织在一起，其中融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和Surf Rock，加上隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词，都是他们标志性的风格。但在当时他们却被主流媒体拒之门外，最终由于乐队领袖Black Francis与贝斯手和歌手Kim Deal的矛盾导致乐队在92年解体。

return.narrative:
Pixies 这条世界线可以从一个核心事实开始：目录数据显示，这个艺人实体下关联着 102 张专辑与 1619 首音乐作品，规模远超“生涯只有六年”这一描述给人的直觉印象 [music-api:artist:98542]。这种数量与时间跨度之间的张力，本身就是继续沿图探索的理由——它提示我们，Pixies 的目录里既有核心录音室作品，也可能包含大量现场、合辑与再版，值得逐条展开。

从年代与场景来看，目录中的艺人简介把 Pixies 定位为上世纪 80 年代末期美国最有影响力的另类摇滚乐队之一，并提到他们属于 4AD 旗下，音乐融合了朋克、Indie Rock、流行乐和 Surf Rock，标志性风格是粗粝咆哮的吉他、时断时续的节奏、和谐的男女合声，以及隐晦怪异、片断式的歌词 [music-api:artist:98542]。同一段简介还指出，他们当时被主流媒体拒之门外，最终因乐队领袖 Black Francis 与贝斯手兼歌手 Kim Deal 的矛盾而在 92 年解体 [music-api:artist:98542]。这些信息共同勾勒出一个“地下/另类场景出身、商业主流接受度有限、内部张力导致终止”的叙事框架，也解释了为什么图中的歌曲节点值得逐一查看：它们正是这一风格与场景的具体载体。

图中的歌曲节点覆盖了不同面向。Where Is My Mind? 与 Where Is My Mind 作为两个独立条目同时存在，都通过 performed_by 关系指向 Pixies [music-api:artist:98542]；这种同曲异名或不同版本并存的情况，本身就是目录层面值得留意的细节。Here Comes Your Man、Hey、The Thing、The Happening、Greens and Blues、All I Think About Now 同样以 performed_by 关系挂在 Pixies 之下 [music-api:artist:98542]。把这些节点放在一起，可以看到一条从早期代表作到较晚作品的目录切片，适合作为继续探索的入口。

影响关系是这条世界线中最值得展开的部分。图中有一条从 Pixies 指向 Nirvana 的 influenced 边 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d]。外部资料对此有更具体的说法：Nirvana 受到 The Melvins，尤其是美国朋克乐队 The Pixies 的影响 [knowledge:chunk:21ba719d1d12c13424cc0502]；另有资料称 Pixies 对 Nirvana 有深远影响，并且 Pixies 在英国拿下三张前十专辑，而在美国连 Billboard 前 60 都尚未进入 [knowledge:chunk:8d38574abe1b22543e32da12]。这组对比说明，Pixies 的影响力路径并不是先在本土主流取得成功、再向外辐射，而更像是在英国等市场先获得认可，再通过后来者对美国另类摇滚产生回响。

把这条影响边放回更大的场景中，还能看到另一层关系：有资料在讨论 Nirvana 的遗产时提出，如果不是 Nirvana，也会有另一支站在 REM、Pixies、The Replacements 和 Sonic Youth 等“巨人”肩上的乐队翻过那道把地下与主流隔开的墙 [knowledge:chunk:9994c86ab814a3c2b8e64546]。同一资料还提到，Nirvana 与 grunge 的崛起在 1994 年的英国产生了反向效果，Britpop 随之兴起 [knowledge:chunk:8d38574abe1b22543e32da12]。这意味着 Pixies 在图中的位置不只是一个被指向的源头，而是连接美国另类摇滚与英国场景变化的一个节点，值得沿着 influenced 边继续追踪。

综合来看，这条世界线的探索价值在于三层叠加：目录层面有 102 张专辑、1619 首作品和多个具体歌曲节点可供展开 [music-api:artist:98542]；风格与场景层面有 4AD、朋克/Indie/Surf Rock 融合、男女合声与片断式歌词等可核实的描述 [music-api:artist:98542]；影响层面则有指向 Nirvana 的明确边，以及关于英美市场接受度差异和 Britpop 反向效应的外部叙述 [knowledge:influence:3d36044aeffb65729063736d][knowledge:chunk:8d38574abe1b22543e32da12]。沿着这些节点与关系继续走，可以把“一支短命乐队为何被反复提及”这个问题拆解成可验证的目录事实与可追溯的影响链条。

sources.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

metadata.source_evidence_content:
Nirvana's legacy extends beyond 1994, of course.

The number of kids who picked up a guitar because of Cobain, or drumsticks to emulate Dave Grohl, or a bass to play the loping lines of Krist Novoselic is innumerable, and continues to this day.

You could argue that if it hadn't been Nirvana, it would have been another band that stood on the shoulders of giants such as REM and Pixies and The Replacements and Sonic Youth, and dived over the wall that kept the underground away from the mainstream.

But in the end, it was Nirvana.

Their influence wasn't just created by their sound or their industry impact though.

The underdog status of Nirvana — the band no-one had heard of who dethroned the King of Pop — made them the band that other up-and-coming bands looked at and went "maybe we could do that".

But 30 years on from Cobain's passing, the music industry is such a different place that it's hard to understand how profound an impact he and his band had.

But listening to the music from the year he died isn't a bad place to start.

sources.title: Kurt Cobain's legacy is evident in the music from the year he died
sources.excerpt:
The grunge band's influence on the UK was less profound — the British music scene was already open to harder-edged sounds.

For example, American alt-rockers Pixies, who had a profound influence on Nirvana, had three top-10 albums in the UK before they even cracked the Billboard top 60.

But the rise of Nirvana and grunge ended up having an oddly inverse effect in England by 1994.

While American guitar music was embracing its abrasiveness, the British equivalent leaned into its Englishness almost as a direct response to the grimness of grunge.

![The band Blur pose for a promo photo](https://live-production.wcms.abc-cdn.net.au/dfe38ee096b7ed74771b1ca749202570?impolicy=wcms_crop_resize&cropH=987&cropW=1481&xPos=71&yPos=0&width=862&height=575)

Blur was one of the British bands that bucked against the US grunge onslaught. (Supplied: EMI/Paul Postle)

As Blur frontman Damon Albarn told Melody Maker in 1993 upon the release of their album Modern Life Is Rubbish: "Our last album killed baggy — this one will kill grunge."

And so rose Britpop, a burgeoning alt-rock sub-genre that would go on to dominate the mid-'90s much like grunge had dominated the first part of the decade.

The Seattle sound was out and Cool Britannia — led by Blur, Oasis, Pulp, Suede, Elastica, Manic Street Preachers and Radiohead — was in.

citations.title: Assessing an American pop icon
citations.excerpt:
- facebook icon

In late 2011, a re-mastered edition of the seminal album Nevermind by pop-punk band Nirvana was released, marking the work’s 20th anniversary.

At the time of its initial release in 1991, the group’s recording label Geffen Records was forced to suspend the production of all other artists on its roster to focus on meeting the demand that the album’s release, bolstered by the hit single “Smells like Teen Spirit,” had generated. As of today, the album has gone multi-platinum in over a dozen countries, as well as being certified diamond (over 10 million copies shipped) in the United States.

![Nevermind](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-neve-250.jpg)

The re-issue of Nevermind provides the listener an opportunity to focus on some of the album’s own weaknesses and strengths, as well as the group’s enduring impact.

Nirvana—consisting of lead vocalist-guitarist Kurt Cobain (1967-1994), bass guitarist Krist (credited as Chris) Novoselic and drummer-guitarist David Grohl—emerged from the “Grunge-rock” scene, a West Coast variant of punk, which originated in Seattle, near the band’s hometown of Aberdeen, Washington, in the late 1980s. Nirvana was influenced by such groups as The Melvins and especially the American punk group, The Pixies.

![Cobain](https://www.wsws.org/images/2012dec/d05-nirv-coba-250.jpg)

Many of the band’s songs are unusually structured, consisting of moments of tense calm that give way to choruses characterized by abrasive, “grungy” vocals and musical accompaniment. Rather than being a superfluous element, this dynamic carried genuine aesthetic and emotional value, with many of these high-intensity switches feeling “of a piece” with the song as a whole, endowing it with an element of needed urgency.
